extracted.intended_audience: prospective MFA applicants; undergraduates and graduate students interested in creative writing
extracted.subtask_description: Catalog overview of the Iowa Writers' Workshop MFA program, its history, notable alumni, and the creative-writing courses offered to undergraduate and graduate students. Useful for prospective students to understand program components and course offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrollment requirement for graduate-level courses
rubrics_metrics.description: Enrollment in some graduate-level courses requires admission to the MFA program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some courses listed are open only to admitted MFA students; other creative-writing courses may be available to non-MFA students (including summer offerings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Culminating project requirement (MFA Thesis / Graduate Project)
rubrics_metrics.description: Course listings include CW:7890 Graduate Project in Creative Writing and CW:7895 MFA Thesis (arranged credit), indicating a culminating creative project is part of graduate study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These arranged-credit courses imply students complete a substantial thesis or project to fulfill degree requirements (details would be on the program website or degree handbook).

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop and seminar-based instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: The program emphasizes workshop courses and seminars in both fiction and poetry (e.g., Fiction Workshop, Poetry Workshop, Undergraduate Writers' Workshop: Fiction/Poetry, Form of Fiction, Form of Poetry, Seminars: Problems in Modern Fiction/Poetry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction is primarily driven by workshopping, with focused seminars on form and problems in modern genres; course titles indicate an emphasis on peer critique, craft study, and close reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific craft emphases reflected in course titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Course titles indicate targeted skills and goals, e.g., CW:4760 The Art of Revision: Rewriting Prose for Clarity and Impact; CW:4745 The Sentence: Strategies for Writing; CW:3002 Writing and Reading Young Adult Fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These titles signal pedagogical priorities such as revision for clarity and impact, sentence-level strategy, genre-specific techniques, and working writers' practice; students can expect instruction and assessment around these craft dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program accessibility for non-MFA students
rubrics_metrics.description: The Creative Writing Program offers courses for students from other programs of study; summer courses are open to undergraduate and graduate students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Undergraduates and non-MFA graduate students can enroll in many creative-writing courses, though some graduate-level classes may require MFA admission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program reputation and historical distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Iowa Writers' Workshop is described as a world-renowned graduate program, founded in 1936, noted as the first U.S. program to offer a degree in creative writing and a model for many contemporary programs; faculty and alumni include numerous major award winners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not a rubric for writing itself, this emphasizes institutional prestige and suggests expectations of high-level mentorship and a historically established workshop pedagogy.
